body.target_estimand: \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\), where \(\tau_P\) is the unique continuous Hölder representative of the conditional causal contrast

sampling_model.units: The records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent under each component law; each diagnostic sample mixture retains one shared nuisance-sign vector across all records.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator is supplied. On arbitrary bounded-outcome datasets the score uses \(V=\operatorname{clip}(2Y-1,-1,1)\); on the binary signed family this equals \(2Y-1\), so the exact core-cell second moment is unchanged. The test averages out the signed nuisance through that family-specific second moment and normalizes each occupied cell by its realized ordered-pair count.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 derive the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE minimax rate, and Section 5 develops the localized higher-order construction.
Section 3 constructs pure-private simple-hypothesis tests from clamped one-record log-likelihood ratios.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad lower bounds through mixture couplings and expected Hamming distance.
Section 4.1, Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16 give a pure-private T-mechanism whose generic finite-cover control contains \(\log|\mathcal P_\eta|\).
The paper constructs central-private U-statistic estimators using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2 give pure-private finite-hypothesis and cover-based selection with costs proportional to \(\log m\) and \(\log|\mathcal C_\alpha|\).
The paper provides composition-based differentially private CATE meta-learners without a sharp pure-private pointwise Hölder minimax frontier.
Theorems 1 and 3 give observational Neyman-orthogonal CATE releases under approximate \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-differential privacy using Gaussian vector or Gaussian-process perturbations.

body.tldr: Unknown propensity can make separated pointwise CATE fibers have identical one-record nuisance mixtures while leaving an exact two-record signal. On a smooth signed binary family inside the unchanged exact-uniform Hölder class, clipping the transformed outcome is inactive and therefore preserves every signed-family moment, while making the pair score valid on all bounded-outcome datasets. The occupancy-normalized sum has per-cell deletion or insertion change at most \(4/3\), replacement sensitivity at most \(8/3\), and supports a finite pure-private test with \(\operatorname{Laplace}(8/(3\epsilon))\) noise and error \(C\exp(-ckp_2a^2b^2)+C\exp(-c\epsilon kp_2ab)\), without a nuisance-cardinality logarithm. This upper/test guarantee is specific to the signed family. Its obstruction and any converse obtained from the embedded subclass transfer to anchor classes containing that subclass, but the full-class upper frontier remains open; the weighted shell functional is only a sufficient certificate for that lift.

project_justification.gap: Simple private tests use additive one-record likelihood increments, while generic private selection and T-mechanisms control finite covers through cardinality terms. The coupled CATE fibers here have intersecting one-record convex hulls, and published results do not supply a nuisance-independent second-order score certificate for arbitrary least-favorable priors over the full Hölder fibers.
project_justification.niche: On the explicit signed family, a higher-order private test uses a signal common to every nuisance profile only when two observations occupy the same public localization cell. Realized occupancy normalization, together with a clipped bounded-outcome mark, yields all-dataset replacement sensitivity at most \(8/3\) and preserves the \(n^2\epsilon\) pair-information balance. This construction is not asserted for general full-class fibers.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs and audits a pair test on a legal smooth signed two-fiber family, proves an explicit pure-private test and risk bound for that family, gives an exact finite two-record diagnostic experiment, and states—without resolving—the full-class lift through one precisely defined weighted shell functional.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024), Theorems 1--2 and Section 5, define the nonprivate Hölder pointwise-CATE benchmark and localized higher-order geometry; those results inform the smooth family but are not private upper comparators. Canonne et al. (2019), Section 3, construct optimal private simple tests from clamped one-record likelihood ratios; the one-record convex-hull obstruction here explains why that additive representation cannot distinguish the displayed composite fibers. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021) provide central-private mixture converses through Hamming transport; converse consequences from the present embedded subclass transfer to any anchor class containing it, but this does not transfer the signed-family upper test. Asi et al. (2024), Section 4.1, Theorem 13, Lemma 15, and Proposition 16, control a pure-private T-mechanism over finite total-variation covers with \(\log|\mathcal P_\eta|\); the present common-orientation pair test avoids catalogue selection only on its explicit signed family and is not a generic strengthening. Bun et al. (2021), Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, give pure-private hypothesis and cover selection with \(\log m\) and \(\log|\mathcal C_\alpha|\) costs. Chaudhuri et al. (2024) stabilize private U-statistics with local Hájek projections, whereas the exact core normalization and shared causal second moment used here are family-specific. Niu et al. (2022) give private CATE meta-learners without a pure-private pointwise Hölder frontier. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025), Theorems 1 and 3, study observational Neyman-orthogonal finite and functional CATE releases under approximate \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-privacy rather than the pure-private composite-fiber problem considered here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The early-kill experiment used \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\), \(n=2\), \(a=b=2/25\), and \(\epsilon=1\). For \(k=1,\ldots,8\), finite nonprivate and private programs were evaluated on all \((4k)^2\) ordered datasets with every one-record replacement edge imposed; the exact symmetry formula was also checked through \(k=12\). These computations are diagnostics, not a proof that randomized response is optimal over all private mechanisms. The formal finite proposition establishes its stated Bayes risk and exact privacy loss only for the specified mechanism. The signed-family asymptotic test additionally requires sparse occupancy \(n\delta^{d/q}\le c\). At \(\delta=r_F\), compatibility requires \(\epsilon\ge c n^{-1+q/d+q/\gamma}\); at \(\delta=r_{\mathrm{pair}}\), asymptotic feasibility requires \(d\ge2q+qd/\gamma\). Dense occupancy is the next unresolved elbow. None of these checks proves the full-class lifting certificate or removes the arbitrary-prior higher-order remainder.
body.honest_scope: The formal contribution is the exact-uniform smooth signed two-fiber family, its one-record convex-hull obstruction, the sparse-occupancy pure-private pair test with clipped marks and \(8/3\) replacement sensitivity, and a specified finite diagnostic experiment. The private upper and risk bounds are strictly signed-family-specific. Only obstruction or converse implications from this embedded subclass transfer upward to an anchor class that contains it. The pair-radius calculation requires \(q<\gamma\) and \(n\delta^{d/q}\le c\); at \(r_F\) this entails \(\epsilon\ge c n^{-1+q/d+q/\gamma}\), while compatibility at \(r_{\mathrm{pair}}\) requires \(d\ge2q+qd/\gamma\). Dense occupancy is a separate elbow. The work does not establish the full-class private minimax frontier: the handle \(H_{\mathrm{pair\mbox{-}lift}}\) merely names a sufficient weighted-shell certificate, and constructing that certificate uniformly over arbitrary least-favorable priors remains open.
body.interpretation: The pair statistic establishes a genuine higher-order escape from the one-record mixture collision on one legal signed subclass. Clipping is a data-domain repair, not a restriction of the model: it leaves binary-family moments unchanged and makes every pair kernel lie in \([-1,1]\). The \(8/3\) global sensitivity comes from at most \(4/3\) change in each of two distinct cells; a within-cell replacement changes the block by at most two. These facts certify the displayed signed-family mechanism. They do not construct stable composite scores for arbitrary least-favorable priors, so \(\mathfrak W_r\) should be read as a sufficient, computable criterion whose full-class realization is the open problem.
